newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends steady as NYMEX heat turns losses.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends steady as NYMEX heat turns losses.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures ended steady and Brent crude oil staged a partial recovery after NYMEX crude and products recovered half, or all in the case of heating oil, of their opening losses, traders said.
The January gas oil contract ended at $230.25 a tonne, up 75 cents, with the Jan/Feb backwardation at $4.25, up $1, as continued cold weather in Europe supported the front month contract.
Opening one cent a gallon losses on NYMEX heating oil led by Tuesday's bearish U.S. stocks report were retraced as players covered shorts left by the early profit taking.

Feb Brent dipped 15 cents on the NYMEX opening to trade 37 cents down at the day's low of $24.22 a barrel, but it too was recovering in late trade to stand 17 cents down at $24.42 cents a barrel as NYMEX crude and gasoline turned round early falls.

Few people were convinced Brent's upside had been broken, but traders said any sign of warmer weather in Europe could prompt Brent to slip further, even though API data showed a 9.47 million barrel draw in U.S. crude oil stocks.
